stem: A company runs a product catalog website on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Viewers are in many countries. The cache hit ratio is low, and the origin instances are overloaded. The cache policy of the distribution includes all query strings, all cookies and the User-Agent header in the cache key. Each catalog page changes only with the value of the lang query string. The team does not want to write or maintain any code for this change. Which combination of steps will raise the cache hit ratio and reduce the origin load with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
keywords: changes only with the value of the lang query string
does not want to write or maintain any code

options.text: Attach a cache policy to the cache behavior that includes only the lang query string in the cache key, with no cookies and no headers.
options.why: AWS says to [forward only the query string parameters](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-cache-hit-ratio-forward-only-needed-values) that change the response.

options.text: Associate a CloudFront function with the viewer request event that removes all cookies, the User-Agent header and every query string except lang.
options.why: It works, because [cache key normalization](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-functions-use-cases) suits CloudFront Functions, but it is code to write and maintain where a policy setting is enough.

options.text: Keep all cookies in the cache key, and add every other viewer header to it, so that each cached copy matches its request more exactly.
options.why: Every extra value splits a page into more copies; AWS says to [forward only specified cookies instead of forwarding all](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-cache-hit-ratio-forward-only-needed-values) cookies.

options.text: Turn on Origin Shield for the origin, and choose the AWS Region that has the lowest latency to the EC2 instances of the catalog.
options.why: Origin Shield is a [centralized caching layer](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-origin-shield-central-cache-layer), placed in [the AWS Region that has the lowest latency](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-origin-shield-choose-lowest-latency-region) to the origin.

options.text: Create an invalidation for the /* path every hour, so that the edge locations keep a fresh copy of every catalog page.
options.why: An invalidation empties the cache, so the next requests go to the origin; AWS says to [use invalidation only in unexpected circumstances](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-invalidate-only-unexpected-use-versioning).
options.misconception: believes that frequent invalidations keep the cache fresh without losing cache hits

explanation: Values in the cache key that do not change the page split it into many separate copies. A cache policy decides what is [included in the cache key](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-cache-policy-controls-cache-key), so a key with only lang raises the hit ratio. With Origin Shield, CloudFront will [route all origin fetches through Origin Shield](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-origin-shield-central-cache-layer), one more cache before the origin.
takeaway: Low hit ratio: shrink the cache key to the values that change the page, then add Origin Shield.
twin: If the stem said "every page is different for each signed-in user" instead: the pages are not cacheable, and the managed CachingDisabled policy is [useful for dynamic content](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-managed-policy-caching-disabled).
